newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean parliament agrees on labour law compromise.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean parliament agrees on labour law compromise.

text.p: A South Korean parliamentary committee has agreed to delay implementation of a controversial section of a new labour law that would allow companies to lay off workers, a committee statement said on Friday.
It also agreed to recognise an outlawed union body that organised almost one month of strikes in protest at passage of the law last December.
However, the committee composed of representatives of all major parties, was still deadlocked on several thorny issues, including payment for union officials and strikers.
The new law, which President Kim Young-sam was forced to return to parliament for revision, would make it illegal for companies to pay full-time union organisers.
It also ruled that companies must not pay workers during the time they are on strike.

The issue of layoffs and free labour union association aroused the greatest passions among opponents of the law, which was rammed through parliament by the ruling New Korea Party with no debate on December 26.
